aboutpara: My name is Sameer Agarwal, and I am a full-time freshman at the University of Texas at Austin, Texas. I'm majoring in computer science and have been developing websites and other projects. I am also learning about Machine Learning, AI, and Applications. Some activities I do include FRC Robotics, Tutoring, and Computer Repair. In my free time, I listen to music, play guitar, and play video games. I hope this website gives you an insight into my journey with Computer Science so far. Thanks for reading!

resume.tagline: 👋  I'm a College student who aspires to be a Software Engineer
resume.description: Experienced Software Engineer Intern at NeuraCities. Proficient in Java, C++, Python, and frameworks such as React and NextJs

bullets: Built an interactive GIS viewer and conversion web app using React, JavaScript, and Leaflet, enabling upload, visualization, and conversion of 7+ geospatial formats
Designed and deployed a production-grade Python GIS data ingestion pipeline actively used by clients to automatically discover municipal geospatial data
Built a universal data discovery system integrating ArcGIS Online, Socrata Discovery Search, CKAN, and ODS
Validated pipeline across 200+ cities in North America and Europe, with the potential to automatically scale to thousands more cities
Designed high-fidelity mockups and user flows in Figma, translating visual concepts into a responsive mobile application to ensure a seamless user experience
Engineered the frontend architecture and high-performance mobile interface using TypeScript, Expo Router, and React Native in collaboration with 5 other developers
Architecting a scalable backend API integrating OpenCV to process user-submitted video footage, automating the extraction of anthropometric measurements for precise figure analysis
Strategizing the implementation of an augmented reality clothing viewer utilizing Apple ARKit and Google Sceneform, enabling users to visualize apparel fit and style on 3D avatars in real-time
Researched the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in cybersecurity and used Python to develop a GAN model to enhance physical security functions.
Trained the model with TensorFlow to authenticate false responses from Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs), achieving an AUC Score of .99.
Authored and submitted a research paper to an IEEE conference detailing the GAN model's success in authenticating false responses, supported by ROC curves and confusion matrices.
Participated in 3 different Robotics Competitions while in Robotics.
Won 3 team awards during participation in Robotics Competitions.
Learned how to use machinery and complete something with a team.
Learned Programming and designed a majority of the robot's code.
Led other programmers and taught them how to code.

I coordinate with other departments to keep tutoring running smoothly.
I host workshops for tutors to improve their skills and also train new tutors
